note: In-sandbox measurement of the C3 single-point-of-failure: is the sample-based lower certificate cheaper than the full join it is meant to avoid? Measured on real IMDb (JOB queries 10a/10b/10c, 7-way joins) at increasing per-table row caps. cost_ratio = lower_cert_time / full_count_time.

unreachable_in_sandbox.reason: 7-way count_join frontier exceeds the sandbox time/memory budget for both the full count and the certificate; needs the local full run

findings.seed_multiplier: The 200-row 2.2x is a 3-seed aggregation overhead, not the certificate itself: with lower_seeds=1 the ratio drops below 1.0. Cost scales ~linearly in seeds, so use 1 seed for the cost-sensitive path and more only when L_hat stability is needed.
findings.scale_trend: At single seed the certificate is ~0.67-0.71x the full-join cost at 2k-5k rows (i.e. ~30% cheaper), because only the largest relation is sub-sampled while the join dominates cost. The ratio is stable, not exploding, across the reachable range.
findings.floor: The certificate's speedup is bounded below by the cost of joining the non-sampled relations; sampling only the largest relation cannot beat that floor. Sampling the cost-dominant relation (not merely the largest by row count) is the design lever to push cost_ratio lower.
findings.verdict: C3 PARTIALLY DE-RISKED in-sandbox: single-seed certificate is cheaper than execution at measurable scales and the trend is favorable. The definitive real-JOB-scale answer requires the local full run (7-way joins blow up past ~20k rows here). This is the W4 kill-gate input.
